day_by_day.morning: Arrival — Flight TP lands at 13:00, so no morning activities scheduled. Use the morning on the plane to rest.
day_by_day.afternoon: After landing at Humberto Delgado Airport around 13:00, take the Metro (Linha Vermelha/Red Line) to the city center — cheapest option at ~€1.65 with a Viva Viagem card. Check in to Lisbon City Stay, freshen up, then take a self-guided walk through Baixa (Downtown Lisbon) and Praça do Comércio. Stroll along the Tagus riverfront, admire the grand Arco da Rua Augusta (free exterior view), and soak in your first impressions of the city.
day_by_day.evening: Head uphill to the Alfama district for a gentle evening wander through its narrow medieval alleyways. Climb to Miradouro das Portas do Sol for a free panoramic sunset view over the rooftops and the Tagus River. End the evening with dinner in Alfama.

meals.breakfast: On the plane or grab a quick pastel de nata (€1.20) and coffee (€0.80) at the airport café upon arrival.
meals.lunch: Pick up a budget-friendly bifana (pork sandwich, ~€2–3) from a local snack bar near Praça do Comércio after arriving in the city center.
meals.dinner: Taberna da Rua das Flores or a local tasca in Alfama — look for a prato do dia (dish of the day) which typically includes soup, main, and bread for €8–10. Try bacalhau à brás (salted cod with eggs and fries).

day_by_day.notes: Buy a Viva Viagem reloadable Metro card at the airport (€0.50 card fee + top up). The Red Line metro from the airport to Baixa-Chiado takes about 25 minutes and costs €1.65 — far cheaper than a taxi (~€15–20). Keep your first evening light as jet lag or travel fatigue may set in.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the National Tile Museum (Museu Nacional do Azulejo) — one of Lisbon's most unique and affordable cultural gems. Explore five centuries of Portugal's iconic decorative azulejo tile art. Entry is €5 (free on the 1st Sunday of each month). Open from 10:00. Take Bus 794 or 718 from the city center (~15 min ride).
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the historic Mouraria neighborhood, the birthplace of Fado music, for a self-guided walk. Explore the colorful streets around Intendente square and visit the free Igreja de Nossa Senhora do Fado. Then walk up to the Castelo de São Jorge — entry is €15 but the surrounding free hilltop viewpoints (Miradouro do Castelo) offer equally stunning views if you want to save money. Consider spending the €15 for the castle if history is a top priority.
day_by_day.evening: Experience the Time Out Market Lisbon Food Tour — spend the evening grazing through Lisbon's iconic food hall at Mercado da Ribeira. Sample dishes from top local chefs at affordable prices. Try a range of small plates: fresh seafood, petiscos (Portuguese tapas), and local wines. Budget €15–20 for a satisfying food tour of the market.

meals.breakfast: At a local pastelaria near the hotel — coffee + pastel de nata + toast (tosta mista) for under €3.50.
meals.lunch: After the Tile Museum, grab lunch at a neighborhood café in the Santa Apolónia or Intendente area. Look for a menu do dia (set lunch) for €8–10 including soup, main course, and a drink.
meals.dinner: Time Out Market Lisbon — graze on small plates from multiple vendors. Budget €15–20 total. Try the ginjinha (cherry liqueur shot, ~€1.50) at a street kiosk nearby afterward.

day_by_day.notes: The National Tile Museum is closed on Mondays — Saturday is perfect. Time Out Market is busiest on weekends, so arrive by 18:30 to beat the dinner rush and get a seat easily. The market is located at Cais do Sodré, easily reachable by Metro (Green Line) or tram.

day_by_day.morning: Take Tram 28E (iconic historic tram, €3 with Viva Viagem card) from Martim Moniz through Alfama, Graça, and up to the Miradouro da Graça — one of Lisbon's best and least crowded viewpoints. Enjoy the panorama over the city and the Tagus. Then walk down through the Graça neighborhood, stopping at the Igreja de São Vicente de Fora (€5 entry, rooftop views included) — a beautiful 17th-century monastery with stunning azulejo panels inside.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Feira da Ladra flea market (open Tuesdays and Saturdays — if today is Sunday, substitute with a visit to the LX Factory Sunday market on Rua Rodrigues de Faria). LX Factory hosts a weekly Sunday market with local artisans, vintage goods, and street food in a converted industrial space — free entry, very budget-friendly. Browse stalls and enjoy the creative atmosphere.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Bairro Alto for an evening of petiscos (Portuguese tapas) bar-hopping. This neighborhood is famous for its lively yet affordable bar scene. Many bars offer free or cheap snacks with drinks. Try a glass of vinho verde (green wine, ~€2–3) or a Super Bock beer (~€1.50) at a local tasca.

meals.breakfast: If it's the 1st Sunday of the month, revisit the National Tile Museum for free. Otherwise, enjoy breakfast at a local café near the hotel — galão (milky coffee) + pastel de nata for €2.50.
meals.lunch: At LX Factory — try the street food stalls for affordable bites: local cheeses, chouriço bread, or a fresh sandwich for €4–6.
meals.dinner: Cervejaria Ramiro (splurge option, ~€25–30) or a more budget-friendly tasca in Bairro Alto with petiscos plates at €3–6 each. Build a meal from 3–4 small plates for under €15.

day_by_day.notes: Tram 28E is a tourist attraction in itself but can get very crowded — board early in the morning to get a seat and avoid pickpockets. Keep belongings secure. LX Factory Sunday market runs from approximately 10:00–19:00.

day_by_day.morning: Full day in Belém — take the train from Cais do Sodré station (€1.65 each way, ~15 min) to Belém station. Start with the Jerónimos Monastery (UNESCO World Heritage Site) — entry is €10 but the church interior is free. The monastery is a breathtaking example of Manueline architecture and houses the tomb of Vasco da Gama. Arrive early (opens 10:00) to beat crowds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk 10 minutes along the riverfront to the iconic Torre de Belém (Tower of Belém) — another UNESCO-listed Manueline masterpiece. Entry is €6. Explore the tower and enjoy views over the Tagus estuary. Nearby, visit the free Padrão dos Descobrimentos (Monument to the Discoveries) exterior and the free riverside promenade. Optionally, visit the Centro Cultural de Belém gardens (free) for a riverside rest.
day_by_day.evening: Return to central Lisbon by train. Head to the Chiado neighborhood for an evening stroll past the historic Livraria Bertrand (world's oldest operating bookshop — free to browse) and the Igreja do Carmo ruins (€5 entry, closes 18:00 — plan accordingly). Enjoy dinner in Chiado or nearby Bairro Alto.

meals.breakfast: The unmissable stop — Pastéis de Belém bakery (Est. 1837), just steps from the monastery. The original pastéis de Belém (custard tarts) cost ~€1.30 each. Have 2–3 with a coffee for a perfect budget breakfast under €6.
meals.lunch: Picnic-style lunch on the Belém riverfront — grab fresh bread, local cheese, and chouriço from a nearby mini-market for €5–7 total. Eat with a view of the Tagus.
meals.dinner: A Cevicheria or local restaurant in Chiado/Bairro Alto — look for a menu do dia or petiscos. Budget €10–14 for a satisfying dinner with a glass of wine.

day_by_day.notes: The Belém Historical Monuments experience covers both the Jerónimos Monastery and Tower of Belém — the highlight of any Lisbon history trip. Combined entry to both is ~€16 but absolutely worth it for history lovers. Buy tickets online in advance to skip queues. The Pastéis de Belém bakery can have long lines — arrive before 10:00 or after 15:00 for shorter waits.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Feira da Ladra open-air flea market at Campo de Santa Clara in Alfama (open Tuesdays and Saturdays, 09:00–18:00). Browse antiques, vintage finds, old books, azulejo tiles, and local curiosities. It's free to enter and perfect for picking up affordable souvenirs. Afterward, visit the nearby Igreja de Santa Engrácia (National Pantheon) for €4 — stunning baroque interior and rooftop views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to areas you loved or explore the Príncipe Real neighborhood — a charming upscale-bohemian district with a lovely garden (Jardim do Príncipe Real, free), independent bookshops, and antique stores. Visit the Museu Nacional de Arte Antiga (National Museum of Ancient Art) on Rua das Janelas Verdes — entry €6, one of Portugal's finest art collections featuring works from the Age of Discovery. Last chance to pick up any souvenirs or local products (tinned fish, wine, ceramics) at budget-friendly shops.
day_by_day.evening: Final evening — splurge slightly on a Fado dinner experience or find a free/low-cost Fado vadio (amateur Fado) performance at a local tasca in Alfama or Mouraria. Some restaurants host live Fado without a cover charge if you dine there (budget €15–20 for dinner). Wrap up with a final ginjinha at A Ginjinha bar near Rossio square (€1.50 per shot) — a Lisbon institution since 1840.

meals.breakfast: Final pastelaria breakfast near the hotel — try a queijada (cheese tart) or bola de Berlim (cream-filled doughnut) for a change, with coffee. Under €4.
meals.lunch: At or near the Feira da Ladra — grab a quick bifana or prego (beef sandwich) from a nearby snack bar for €2.50–4, or sit down at a local tasca for a menu do dia at €8–10.
meals.dinner: A farewell dinner at a traditional Alfama tasca with Fado atmosphere. Look for restaurants on Rua de São João da Praça or Rua dos Remédios. Order grilled sardines (sardinhas assadas, seasonal and iconic in May) or caldo verde (green soup) with a main for €12–16 including a glass of wine.

day_by_day.notes: May is the start of sardine season in Portugal — grilled sardines are a must-try and very affordable at local tascas. For Fado vadio (free/informal Fado), ask your hostel or hotel for current recommendations as venues change. Pack light souvenirs: tinned sardines/fish (€2–5), local wine (€4–8 at a supermarket), or a small azulejo tile (€3–8 at the flea market). Keep receipts for VAT refund eligibility if applicable.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Lisbon Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Clear customs, collect luggage, and take the Aerobus or Metro (Red Line to Green Line) to central Lisbon. Check in to Lisbon City Stay and freshen up.
day_by_day.afternoon: After settling in, take a leisurely self-guided walk through Baixa-Chiado, Lisbon's historic downtown grid. Stroll Rua Augusta, cross Praça do Comércio by the Tagus River, and soak in the city's grand Pombaline architecture. Stop at the iconic Elevador de Santa Justa for panoramic rooftop views over the city.
day_by_day.evening: Head to the Bairro Alto neighborhood for dinner, then explore the lively streets on foot. This is a great first-night introduction to Lisbon's relaxed evening culture.

meals.breakfast: Grab a snack at the airport or a quick pastel de nata and coffee at a café near the hotel upon arrival.
meals.lunch: Light meal at a tasca (traditional tavern) near Praça do Comércio — try a bifana (pork sandwich) or a prego roll for a quick, authentic, budget-friendly bite (~€8–12).
meals.dinner: Dinner at Taberna da Rua das Flores in Bairro Alto — a beloved mid-range spot serving traditional Portuguese petiscos (small plates) like cured meats, bacalhau, and seasonal vegetables (~€20–28 per person).

day_by_day.notes: Day 1 is intentionally light given the 13:00 arrival. Avoid over-scheduling to prevent fatigue. Validate your Metro/transport card (Viva Viagem) at the airport for easy travel throughout the trip. Weather in Lisbon in mid-May is typically warm and sunny (18–24°C), ideal for walking.

day_by_day.morning: Start the day with the Alfama District Walking Tour & Fado Show (morning portion). Join a guided walking tour through Lisbon's oldest and most atmospheric neighborhood — wind through medieval alleyways, visit the Miradouro da Graça viewpoint, and explore the area around the Sé Cathedral and São Jorge Castle. The guide will share stories of Moorish history, the 1755 earthquake, and the birth of Fado.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring Alfama independently after the tour. Visit the Igreja de São Vicente de Fora and the Panteão Nacional (National Pantheon) — both are within walking distance and offer rich historical context. Browse the antique and flea market stalls at Feira da Ladra (open Tuesdays and Saturdays) if timing aligns.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Alfama for the Fado Show component of the experience. Settle into a traditional Fado house for an intimate, soulful performance of Portugal's iconic music genre, paired with wine and local appetizers.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel or a nearby pastelaria — coffee, fresh orange juice, and a croissant or tosta mista (~€4–7).
meals.lunch: Lunch at A Cevicheria or a simpler local restaurant in Alfama — try grilled sardines or caldo verde (green soup) with crusty bread (~€12–18 per person).
meals.dinner: Dinner included as part of the Fado Show experience, or dine beforehand at Restaurante Zé da Mouraria, a no-frills Alfama classic with generous portions of bacalhau à brás and grilled fish (~€15–22 per person).

day_by_day.notes: Book the Alfama Walking Tour & Fado Show in advance as evening Fado sessions fill up quickly, especially on weekends. Wear comfortable shoes — Alfama's cobblestone streets are steep and uneven. Bring a light jacket for the evening.

day_by_day.morning: Spend the morning at the National Tile Museum (Museu Nacional do Azulejo), located in a beautifully converted 16th-century convent in the Xabregas neighborhood (15-min taxi or Uber from central Lisbon). Explore five centuries of Portugal's iconic azulejo tile art, including a stunning 23-meter panoramic tile panel depicting pre-earthquake Lisbon. Allow 2–2.5 hours.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Belém (25-min Tram 15E or Uber) for the Belém Historical Monuments experience. Visit the UNESCO-listed Jerónimos Monastery, a breathtaking example of Manueline Gothic architecture, and walk along the riverfront to the Tower of Belém. Also explore the nearby Monument to the Discoveries.
day_by_day.evening: Relax with a sunset walk along the Belém waterfront, then head back toward central Lisbon or Cais do Sodré for dinner.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at a café near the hotel — try a queijada (cheese tart) or a croissant with coffee (~€4–6).
meals.lunch: The unmissable stop: Pastéis de Belém bakery, just steps from the monastery, for the original and legendary pastel de nata fresh from the oven with cinnamon and powdered sugar (~€2–4 for pastries; pair with a coffee). For a fuller lunch, grab a sandwich or light meal at a nearby café.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Tasca do Chico or a riverside restaurant in Cais do Sodré — try arroz de marisco (seafood rice) or grilled sea bass with potatoes and salad (~€18–25 per person).

day_by_day.notes: The National Tile Museum is closed on Mondays — if this is an issue, swap with another activity and visit the museum on Tuesday or Wednesday instead. Jerónimos Monastery has a small entrance fee (~€10); arrive early to avoid queues. Tram 15E to Belém can be crowded — consider an Uber for comfort.

day_by_day.morning: Join the Mouraria & Intendente Neighborhood Food & History Walk. Discover Lisbon's multicultural Moorish quarter — the historic birthplace of Fado — with a knowledgeable guide. Explore Largo do Intendente, sample street food from diverse cultures (Indian spices, African flavors, Portuguese classics), and learn about the neighborhood's fascinating layered history from Moorish rule to modern-day gentrification.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Time Out Market Lisbon Food Tour in Cais do Sodré. Spend 2–3 hours grazing through Lisbon's celebrated food hall, sampling dishes from top local chefs — from grilled octopus and Alentejo pork to artisan cheeses, craft beer, and ginjinha. A perfect complement to the morning's food focus.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the LX Factory, a trendy creative hub in a repurposed 19th-century industrial complex in Alcântara. Browse independent boutiques, street art, and live music (especially vibrant on Tuesday evenings). Wind down with a cocktail at one of the rooftop bars.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast included or nearby café near hotel — galão (milky coffee) with a torrada (thick toast with butter) (~€3–5).
meals.lunch: Tastings are built into both the Mouraria Food Walk and Time Out Market tour — graze throughout the morning and early afternoon. Budget ~€15–25 for additional tastings at Time Out Market.
meals.dinner: Dinner at LX Factory's Rio Maravilha restaurant or a nearby Alcântara spot — enjoy creative Portuguese cuisine with rooftop Tagus River views (~€22–30 per person).

day_by_day.notes: Day 4 is your most food-focused day — pace yourself across both experiences to avoid overindulging early. The Mouraria walk typically runs 2–3 hours; book in advance. Time Out Market is busiest at lunchtime — visit mid-afternoon for a more relaxed experience. LX Factory is most lively on Sundays but has regular evening events on weekdays too.

day_by_day.morning: Dedicate the final morning to any missed highlights or personal favorites revisited. Recommended: explore the Príncipe Real neighborhood — a charming, upscale residential area with antique shops, independent bookstores, a weekend organic market, and the beautiful Jardim do Príncipe Real. Visit the Museu Nacional de Arte Antiga (National Museum of Ancient Art) nearby for Portuguese Renaissance and maritime-era masterpieces.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a relaxed walk along the Ribeira waterfront promenade from Cais do Sodré to Terreiro do Paço. Stop at a miradouro (viewpoint) — Miradouro de Santa Catarina (Adamastor) is ideal for a final panoramic view of the Tagus. Pick up last-minute souvenirs: quality Portuguese wine, tinned fish (conservas), or azulejo tiles at specialty shops in Chiado.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner in Chiado or Bairro Alto — celebrate the trip with a proper Portuguese sit-down meal.

meals.breakfast: Final breakfast at a beloved local pastelaria — try Confeitaria Nacional near Rossio for pastries and coffee in a historic 19th-century setting (~€5–8).
meals.lunch: Light lunch at a miradouro café or picnic-style from a local deli — grab cheese, cured meats, olives, and a bottle of Vinho Verde (~€10–15).
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at Cervejaria Ramiro (a Lisbon institution for seafood — prawns, lobster, clams) or Alma restaurant in Chiado for refined modern Portuguese cuisine (~€30–45 per person for a special send-off).

day_by_day.notes: Check your departure details and arrange airport transport in advance. Lisbon Airport is 20–30 minutes from the center by Metro or taxi. Leave buffer time on Day 5 if your flight departs the same evening. Príncipe Real's organic market runs on Saturdays — if your schedule allows a Saturday morning here, it's highly recommended. Consider purchasing a ginjinha (cherry liqueur) as a classic Lisbon souvenir.

day_by_day.evening: Return to central Lisbon. Enjoy a relaxed evening exploring the Príncipe Real neighborhood — Lisbon's most refined quarter — browsing antique shops and art galleries. Dine at an elegant riverside restaurant with views over the Tagus.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast followed by the iconic warm pastéis de nata at Pastéis de Belém bakery mid-morning
meals.lunch: Lunch at Feitoria (Michelin-starred) in Belém — an exceptional contemporary Portuguese restaurant inside the Altis Belém Hotel with stunning riverside terrace views
meals.dinner: Dinner at Tasca do Chico in Príncipe Real or Taberna da Rua das Flores — intimate, reservation-only Portuguese tavern serving heritage recipes: slow-roasted suckling pig, clam cataplana, and aged Douro reds

day_by_day.notes: Book a private guide for Jerónimos Monastery to access deeper historical context. Belém is best explored on foot between monuments. The Pastéis de Belém bakery can have queues — arrive early or send your guide ahead. Private car recommended for the Belém day trip.

day_by_day.morning: Time Out Market Lisbon Food Tour: Spend a curated morning at Lisbon's iconic gourmet food hall with a private food guide. Go beyond the tourist surface — your expert will navigate you through the market's best stalls featuring dishes from the city's top chefs. Taste everything from freshly shucked Algarve oysters and grilled chouriço to creative petiscos and artisan Portuguese wines.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Museu Nacional de Arte Antiga (National Museum of Ancient Art) — Portugal's most important art museum. Explore masterworks including Nuno Gonçalves' celebrated Panels of Saint Vincent and a remarkable collection of Portuguese gold and silverwork, Asian decorative arts brought back during the Age of Discovery, and European Old Masters.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset at Miradouro da Graça — one of Lisbon's best-kept secret viewpoints, less crowded than touristy Portas do Sol, offering golden-hour views over the castle and the Tagus. End with a luxurious farewell-to-the-day dinner at one of Lisbon's most celebrated restaurants.

meals.breakfast: Light breakfast at the hotel before the market tour
meals.lunch: The Time Out Market food tour serves as a progressive tasting lunch — oysters, charcuterie, bacalhau croquettes, grilled fish, and local pastries with wine pairings
meals.dinner: Dinner at Eleven (Michelin-starred, Chef Joachim Koerper) on Parque Eduardo VII — elegant contemporary European cuisine with floor-to-ceiling views over Lisbon's skyline and the Tagus; exceptional wine cellar with 400+ Portuguese and international labels

day_by_day.notes: The Time Out Market food tour is best arranged with a private guide for a more exclusive, curated experience — avoid peak lunchtime crowds. The Museu Nacional de Arte Antiga is closed on Mondays in some seasons — verify opening hours with concierge and substitute with Museu do Azulejo revisit or Calouste Gulbenkian Museum if needed.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided visit to the Castelo de São Jorge (St. George's Castle) — Lisbon's iconic Moorish hilltop fortress with commanding 360-degree views over the city, the Tagus, and the distant Serra de Sintra mountains. Explore the archaeological site revealing layers of civilization from Phoenician traders to Moorish rulers to Portuguese kings. Enjoy a peaceful moment at the castle's resident peacock gardens.
day_by_day.afternoon: Leisurely afternoon for personal exploration and luxury shopping in Chiado — visit heritage Portuguese brands such as Vista Alegre (fine porcelain), Claus Porto (artisan soaps and perfumes), and Luvaria Ulisses (hand-stitched gloves since 1925). Alternatively, arrange a private wine tasting experience at a Chiado wine bar specializing in rare Douro, Alentejo, and Vinho Verde labels.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner at a premier Lisbon restaurant celebrating the finest of Portuguese cuisine. Pack, arrange a luxury private transfer for departure, and enjoy a final glass of vintage Port on the hotel terrace.

meals.breakfast: Full gourmet hotel breakfast — linger over freshly squeezed orange juice, smoked salmon, regional cheeses, warm bread, and espresso
meals.lunch: Lunch at Solar dos Presuntos in Rossio — a Lisbon institution since 1974 beloved by locals and visiting dignitaries alike, celebrated for traditional northern Portuguese cuisine: roasted kid, smoked meats, and rich bean stews
meals.dinner: Grand farewell dinner at Loco (Michelin-starred, Chef Alexandre Silva) — one of Lisbon's most avant-garde dining experiences, offering a bold 20-course tasting menu that deconstructs and reimagines Portuguese culinary heritage with theatrical flair and exceptional Portuguese wine pairings

day_by_day.notes: Book Castelo de São Jorge early-morning entry to enjoy the views before tour groups arrive. Confirm departure transfer with hotel concierge the evening before. Consider purchasing artisan souvenirs (azulejo tiles, Port wine, Claus Porto products) during the afternoon shopping — the hotel can arrange secure packing and shipping if needed.
